title: Interpretability
tagline: Probing, the residual stream, circuits, superposition, sparse features and steering
summary: What computations happen inside a language model? This course covers probing and attribution, the residual-stream view of Transformers, circuits such as induction heads, superposition, sparse dictionary learning of features, causal interventions and steering, and the open problems of understanding large models.

chapters.title: Goals and methods of interpretability
chapters.summary: Behavioural, attributional and mechanistic approaches, and what an explanation should achieve.

chapters.title: Probing and attribution
chapters.summary: Linear probes, saliency, attention analysis and their pitfalls.

chapters.title: The residual stream
chapters.summary: Transformers as sums of paths, the logit lens and reading intermediate predictions.

chapters.title: Circuits
chapters.summary: Induction heads, indirect-object identification and reverse-engineering small mechanisms.

chapters.title: Superposition and polysemanticity
chapters.summary: Why neurons mix many features, and toy models of superposition.

chapters.title: Sparse dictionary learning
chapters.summary: Sparse autoencoders, transcoders and dictionaries of features in large models.

chapters.title: Causal interventions and steering
chapters.summary: Activation patching, ablations and steering vectors.

chapters.title: Open problems in interpretability
chapters.summary: Scaling interpretability, the faithfulness of explanations and uses for safety.
